summary: Proxy handoff jitter and NVMe IO spikes causing sustained 5xx bursts and runtime restart cascade on embedding/streaming routes
description: Starting at ~13:05 UTC customer Vidra reported repeated 5xx errors for mixed embedding + streaming traffic. Error volume rose rapidly and correlated with a spike of accept-queue and TLS handshake timeouts at the ingress proxy. Upstream serving runtimes entered repeated restart cycles (OOM/segfault-like exits) on several GPUs. Impact: multiple customer endpoints experienced timeouts and 502/503 responses; critical paths for real-time embeddings and chat degraded. This ticket captures the triage, interim mitigations, and next steps.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a dedicated tenant in us-east, send mixed workload: concurrent embedding bulk upload (batch size ~512 amortized) plus 100 low-latency chat streaming sessions.
2) Observe ingress proxy accept-queue depth and TLS handshake latencies during burst (load generator used: k6 + custom embed uploader).
3) Watch apigw logs for consecutive 502/504 and upstream resets; correlate with runtime syslogs and NVMe iostat metrics.
4) Repeat with prewarm disabled to replicate the warmup-induced IO pattern.
observed_logs: [2026-03-14T13:05:16Z] ingress-proxy[worker-7]: half-closed socket detected, backlog=256, errno=EPIPE
[2026-03-14T13:05:22Z] runtime[gpu-3]: emergency restart triggered (watchdog), pid=22987 exit_code=137
investigation_notes: 13:10 UTC - Support: initial customer report captured; elevated 5xx, streaming disconnects and embed failures. Opened incident and notified SRE.
13:18 UTC - SRE: confirmed apigw accept_queue growth and increased TLS handshake latency on multiple frontends; socket halfclose pattern seen in ingress-proxy logs.
13:25 UTC - Observed NVMe iowait spike on ephemeral nodes hosting serving runtime that coincided with runtime restarts; background nvme compaction job scheduled at 13:04 on that shard.

13:30 UTC - Hypothesis A: prefetch/warmup + bulk embedding uploads create high disk IO and increased latency, triggering ingress backpressure and causing apigw to mark upstream unhealthy, leading to retry storms and runtime crash loops.
13:33 UTC - Hypothesis B: proxy handoff jitter leaves half-closed sockets leading to connection pileup; runtime connection acceptance stalls and watchdog triggers restarts.
13:40 UTC - Correlation seen between customer bulk embed requests and nvme-background-compact events; other tenants with heavy small-batch streaming also impacted but to lesser degree.
13:45 UTC - Product: model prefetch and KV cache warm paths execute disk-backed checkpoint reads on scale-up; this overlaps with customer bulk upload pattern and increases IO.
13:55 UTC - Reproduced locally in staging with controlled nvme compaction enabled and large embed upload; accept-queue grows and runtime restarts within ~30s.
timeline: 13:05 - First customer alerts received; 5xx spike starts.
13:10 - Incident declared; paging SRE (oncall: Diego A.).
13:20 - Initial mitigation: applied conservative rate-limit (50 rps) on Vidra's embedding route via apigw route-level throttling.
13:28 - Shifted Vidra traffic to fallback deployment pool (weight=10%) to reduce load on affected shard.
13:33 - Disabled background NVMe compaction on affected nodes to test correlation.
13:36 - Observed partial recovery: accept-queue reduced from 1024 -> 120 over 90s; runtime restarts dropped but not eliminated.
13:50 - Temporary circuit-breaker rule added at apigw for streaming route to fail fast on backpressure and avoid retry storms.
14:05 - Customer notified of partial mitigation and to expect degraded throughput until full root cause remediation.
14:30 - Incident escalated for permanent scheduler/runtime changes; engineering ETA requested.
15:00 - Open follow-up PR created to add IO-aware prewarm scheduling: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4273
mitigation: Applied immediate route-level throttling for Vidra embedding endpoints (50 rps) to limit burst amplitude.
Shifted a portion of customer traffic to a fallback pool and reduced weight on affected shard to 5% for safety.
Disabled nvme background compaction on impacted hosts temporarily to reduce iowait.
Enabled apigw circuit-breaker on streaming route to fail-fast and prevent hedged retry amplification.
Instructed customer to pause large parallel bulk-upload jobs while we stabilize cluster.
Runbook note: increased prewarm concurrency to avoid synchronous disk reads during first request where safe.

next_steps: Engineering to implement IO-aware prewarm and staggered KV checkpoint reads (PR 4273) — owner: runtime team, ETA 3 days.
Add persistent metric alert for NVMe avg_iowait > 200ms correlated with apigw accept_queue_growth.
Permanent change to apigw: implement smarter backoff with per-tenant fail-fast to avoid retry amplification; owner: apigw team, ETA 7 days.
Schedule controlled disk maintenance windows for compaction on low-traffic periods and add isolation for prefetch workloads.
Post-incident: runbook update and postmortem to be posted to Confluence within 72 hours.
